title: Leek, Potato and Thyme Focaccia
changes_from_base: Butter and oil in the tin; topped with softened leeks, thin potato and thyme with a little grated cheese.
summary: A buttery-bottomed focaccia topped with sweet softened leeks, thin potatoes, thyme and a little hard cheese.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: medium leeks, white and pale green parts, thinly sliced and rinsed
waxy potatoes, halved lengthways and sliced into thin half-moons
pecorino or Parmesan-style hard cheese, finely grated

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Combine the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 2 tbsp oil, mix to a soft, sticky dough and rest 15 min.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Fold the dough from four sides every 30 min, four times, until it is smooth and full of bubbles.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Rub the tin with the soft butter, then pour in 2 tbsp oil; the butter browns the base and the oil keeps it from catching. Add the dough, turn it over, cover and leave 1 h to puff, pressing it to the corners halfway.

steps.title: Leeks
steps.text: Cook the leeks in the butter and 1 tbsp oil over medium-low heat 10-12 min, until soft and sweet but not browned. Cool a little, then stir in the potato slices and thyme.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Dimple the dough, spread the leek and potato evenly over it, scatter with the cheese and grind over the pepper.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 30-35 min, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden at the edges; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 15 min before cutting.

tips: Rinse the sliced leeks well; grit hides between the layers.
Cook the leeks gently; if they brown they turn bitter.
A common mistake is spreading hot leeks on the dough, which knocks the air out; let them cool first.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat at 200 °C for 6-8 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
